newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks rebound in early trade after easier open.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks rebound in early trade after easier open.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rebounded from an easier opening and were slightly higher on Tuesday morning, but trading was quiet ahead of U.S. congressional testimony from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was up 59 points, or 0.38 percent, to 15,595. It opened at a low of 15,486.09 on the weakness of HSBC.
"Continued selling pressure is seen on HSBC but the better performance of other banks helped the index," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
Investors bought banks on hopes of better interim earnings to be announced in August, brokers said.
HSBC eased HK$1.00 to HK$261.00 after recovering from a low of HK$259.00.
But its unit Hang Seng Bank rose HK$0.50 to HK$115.50 and Bank of East Asia added HK$0.10 to HK$33.00.
Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said Greenspan's testimony was expected to have limited impact on the Hong Kong market.
"The latest U.S. economic figures were pretty mixed with no clear direction so I believe the chance for an interest rate rise in the short term is small," he said.
Brokers said trading was volatile but lacked impetus.
Blue chips were mixed with Cheung Kong easing HK$0.75 to HK$73.75 but China Light up HK$0.40 to HK$44.40.
Individual H-shares surged on restructuring hopes which broght the Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index up four points, or 0.42 percent, to 1,138.
Zhenhai surged HK$0.45 to HK$3.85 and Chengdu Telecom rose HK$0.14 to HK$1.55.
Light profit-taking was seen on red chips as mainland buyers were taking a breather, brokers said.
